curation.lead:
Zachary David Witkoff, born May 21, 1993, is the son of Steve Witkoff, the Trump administration's Special Envoy for Middle East Peace. He serves as CEO of World Liberty Financial (WLFI), the Trump family's cryptocurrency venture, and as Chairman of ALT5 Sigma Corp (ALTS), a publicly traded fintech company that holds approximately 7.5 percent of the total WLFI token supply. [Finding #5829] [Finding #5840] He is also CEO of SC Financial Technologies LLC, the entity that co-owns the USD1 stablecoin brand with WLFI, and the proposed president and chairman of World Liberty Trust Company, which has applied for a national trust bank charter with the OCC. [Connection #2504] [Connection #2541]

Witkoff co-founded WLFI alongside Zachary Folkman and Chase Herro. The SEC Form D lists the Trump family -- Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., and Eric Trump -- as promoters [Finding #3839]. Under the WLFI revenue structure, the Trump family receives 75 percent of net proceeds from token sales and stablecoin profits; by December 2025, the Trumps had profited over $1 billion while holding $3 billion in unsold tokens. [Finding #5829] Zachary operates these ventures while his father simultaneously conducts diplomacy with the same Gulf states whose sovereign wealth vehicles have invested billions in WLFI-adjacent deals. [Finding #5831]

FEC records document Zachary Witkoff's political donations totaling approximately $313,000, heavily concentrated on Trump-aligned and pro-cryptocurrency candidates. [Finding #3796] His listed employer on FEC filings shifted from the Witkoff Group (VP Development) through Witkoff Capital (Family Office) to World Liberty Financial (CEO), tracing his career arc from the family real estate business into the crypto-financial sphere. [Finding #3731]
curation.system_role: Zachary Witkoff occupies the operational center of a structure in which a presidential family's cryptocurrency venture intersects with the diplomatic portfolio of his own father, creating a configuration where the CEO of the venture negotiates deals with foreign state-backed entities in the same jurisdictions where his father conducts official government negotiations, without formal separation or independent oversight.

sections.title: World Liberty Financial and Stablecoin Operations
sections.content:
Zachary Witkoff is CEO of World Liberty Financial (WLFI), a DeFi protocol he co-founded with Zachary Folkman and Chase Herro. The SEC Form D filed October 30, 2024, lists the Trump family members -- Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., and Eric Trump -- as promoters alongside Steve Witkoff and Zachary Witkoff [Finding #3839]. The WLFI token was offered under Rule 506(c) to accredited investors, with the Trump family's DT Marks DEFI LLC receiving 75 percent of net protocol revenue. The Witkoff family receives its share through WC Digital Fi LLC. By December 2025, total Trump family profits exceeded $1 billion, with an additional $3 billion in unsold tokens. [Finding #5829]

WLFI launched the USD1 stablecoin in March 2025, backed by US treasuries. [Finding #5829] The stablecoin is co-owned by SC Financial Technologies LLC, of which Zachary Witkoff is CEO. In January 2026, Witkoff personally visited Pakistan to sign a memorandum of understanding for USD1 integration with the country's financial system. [Connection #2369] [Connection #2504] He also serves as the proposed president and chairman of World Liberty Trust Company, which filed an application with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC application 2026-Charter-344521) for a national trust bank charter. [Connection #2541]

The Folkman and Herro partnership predates WLFI: the two co-founded 17 or more companies since 2013, including Nexus Group in the US Virgin Islands and Dough Finance, a DeFi protocol. Chase Herro donated $746,000 to Trump PACs in July 2024 before co-founding WLFI with the Trump family as promoters. Steve Witkoff served as the bridge, introducing Herro and Folkman to the Trump family. [Connection #2178] [Connection #2174]

sections.title: ALT5 Sigma Corp and Crypto Enterprise Expansion
sections.content:
Zachary Witkoff was appointed Chairman of ALT5 Sigma Corp (ALTS, CIK 0000862861) in August 2025 and filed a Form 3 initial statement of beneficial ownership with the SEC on November 13, 2025. [Finding #3720] ALT5 Sigma, based in Las Vegas, Nevada, is a fintech company providing blockchain-powered tokenization, trading, clearing and settlement, payment processing, and digital asset safekeeping through its ALT5 Pay and ALT5 Prime platforms. [Finding #5840] Its SIC code changed from 6221 (Commodity Contracts Dealers/Brokers) to 2834 in 2025, suggesting a business pivot. [Finding #5839]

Concurrent with Witkoff's appointment, Eric Trump joined the ALT5 board (later redesignated as a board observer to comply with Nasdaq rules). ALT5 simultaneously announced a $1.5 billion registered direct offering and concurrent private placement to initiate a "World Liberty Financial $WLFI Treasury Strategy," resulting in ALT5 holding approximately 7.5 percent of the total WLFI token supply. [Finding #5840] The DEF 14A proxy statement filed February 3, 2026, proposes electing Witkoff alongside Tony Isaac, Zak Folkman, Nael Hajjar, John Bitar, Dr. Adel ElMessiry, and Tim Stanley to the board. [Finding #3720] [Connection #2165]

Jon Isaac, former CEO of JanOne Inc (now ALT5 Sigma), has been under SEC fraud charges since 2021 for inflating earnings and secret stock sales. He left before the 2024 rebrand but retains over one million ALT5 shares, and his brother Tony Isaac was appointed Acting CEO in November 2025.

sections.title: Gulf State Deals and Conflict of Interest
sections.content:
In May 2025, Zachary Witkoff appeared alongside Eric Trump in Abu Dhabi to announce that MGX, a UAE state-backed fund, would invest $2 billion in Binance using WLFI's USD1 stablecoin tokens. [Finding #5831] This announcement occurred while his father Steve Witkoff served as Trump's Special Envoy to the Middle East, conducting active diplomacy with the same Gulf states. Steve Witkoff's financial disclosure shows he continued to retain WLFI cryptocurrency assets ten months into government service. [Finding #5831]

Separately, Aryam Investment 1, an entity linked to UAE national security adviser Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, acquired 49 percent of WLFI for $500 million. Eric Trump signed that contract on January 16, 2025, four days before the inauguration. At least $31 million from that deal flowed to Witkoff-affiliated entities through WC Digital Fi LLC.

The New York Times reported that Steve Witkoff's involvement in a multibillion-dollar AI project between the United States and the UAE coincided with WLFI negotiating its own multibillion-dollar deal with an Emirati state venture firm. [Finding #5831] Congressional records document concerns raised by multiple Democratic lawmakers: Senator Schiff demanded answers on the failure to divest WLFI crypto assets, House Foreign Affairs Democrats called for investigation of what they termed "sketchy business dealings," the House Select Committee on CCP sent a letter to Zachary Witkoff on February 4, 2026, and Senator Blumenthal sent a HSGAC inquiry on May 6, 2025 [Finding #3839]. According to OpenSanctions, Zachary Witkoff is classified as role.rca (Relative or Close Associate of a Politically Exposed Person) [Finding #3839].

sections.title: Political Donations and Pro-Crypto Funding
sections.content:
FEC records show Zachary Witkoff's political donations totaling approximately $313,000. The largest single contribution was $100,000 to Trump Victory on October 26, 2020, accompanied by $35,500 to the RNC on the same date. [Finding #3718] [Finding #5830] Additional contributions include $16,500 to JD Vance campaigns through Vance Victory (2023-2024), $9,400 to JD Vance for Senate, $20,000 across Colorado and Arizona Republican parties, and $7,000 to Morris for Senate in August 2025 with employer listed as World Liberty Financial and occupation CEO. [Finding #3796] [Connection #2230]

A series of donations on September 30, 2024, totaling $26,400, went to pro-cryptocurrency Senate candidates: $13,200 to Republicans for a Pro-Crypto Senate Majority, plus $3,300 each to Rogers for Senate, Sam Brown for Nevada, Friends of Dave McCormick, and Bernie Moreno for Senate. [Finding #3825] These donations predated the public launch of WLFI and suggest the Witkoff family was building relationships with pro-cryptocurrency legislators before the Trump crypto venture became publicly known. Witkoff also made one donation of $2,900 to Ken Russell for Florida in 2021, a Democratic candidate. [Finding #5830]

The employer field on FEC filings traces Witkoff's professional trajectory: through September 2023, he listed "The Witkoff Group" with occupation "Vice President Development." By April 2024, filings show "Witkoff Capital" with occupation "Family Office." By August 2025, the employer shifted to "World Liberty Financial" with occupation "CEO." A misspelling -- "Whtikoff Group" -- appears on the September 2024 filings. [Finding #3731] An examination of corporate registrations across eight jurisdictions did not locate a "Witkoff Capital" entity, suggesting it may operate under a different legal structure [Finding #3822].

sections.title: Corporate Entities and Shell Structure
sections.content:
Beyond WLFI and ALT5, Zachary Witkoff manages at least two Florida LLCs formed in 2025: Andie DC LLC (L25000093601), formed March 5, 2025, and Fortivis LLC (L25000461213), formed October 9, 2025. Both are registered at 4400 Biscayne Boulevard Suite 900, Miami -- the same address as the Witkoff Group headquarters. [Finding #3728] [Finding #3827] A companion entity, Charles DC LLC (L25000093610), lists Alex Witkoff as manager at the same address. [Finding #3728]

The "DC" in the entity names could reference Washington, D.C., though the purpose of these LLCs has not been publicly disclosed. The name "Fortivis" does not appear in other public records. [Finding #3728] These formations occurred during the period when Zachary Witkoff was simultaneously expanding WLFI operations and assuming the ALT5 chairmanship, while his father served as Special Envoy. [Finding #3827]

"Witkoff Capital," listed as Zachary Witkoff's employer on FEC filings in 2021-2024 with occupation "Family Office," was not located in an examination of corporate registries across New York, Florida, New Jersey, Wyoming, Texas, Nevada, Puerto Rico, or the US Virgin Islands, suggesting it may function as an unregistered DBA, trust, or foreign entity [Finding #3822].

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
Steve Witkoff is Zachary's father and the structural connector between the Witkoff family, the Trump family, and the WLFI venture. Steve is named as a Promoter on the WLFI Form D while simultaneously serving as Special Envoy to the Middle East. The family's WLFI revenue flows through WC Digital Fi LLC. [Connection #2185]

Zachary Folkman co-founded WLFI with Witkoff and serves alongside him on the WLF Holdco LLC Board of Managers and on the ALT5 Sigma Corp board. Folkman is also an Executive Officer, Director, and Promoter of WLFI, with DT Marks DEFI LLC (Trump) receiving 75 percent of net revenue and Axiom Management Group LLC (Folkman and Herro) receiving the remainder. [Connection #2174] [Connection #2188]

Chase Herro is the third co-founder, also serving on the WLF Holdco Board of Managers. Herro and Folkman have co-founded 17 or more companies since 2013. Steve Witkoff introduced Herro to the Trump family, and WC Digital Fi LLC (Witkoff) receives 50 percent of the Herro/Folkman WLFI share. [Connection #2178]

Witkoff's political donation pattern shows a sustained financial relationship with JD Vance, including approximately $20,900 across Vance Victory, JD Vance for Senate, and Working for Ohio between September 2023 and April 2024. [Connection #2230] Vance's own network includes Peter Thiel, who served as mentor, employer (at Mithril Capital), backer of Narya Capital, and $15 million donor to Vance's Senate campaign.

open_questions: What is the purpose of Fortivis LLC and Andie DC LLC, the two Florida LLCs formed in 2025 at the Witkoff Group address, and do they have any connection to WLFI operations, Gulf State investments, or Washington D.C. real estate?

What entity is 'Witkoff Capital,' listed as Zachary Witkoff's employer on FEC filings from 2021-2024 but not found in corporate registrations across eight jurisdictions? Is it an unregistered DBA, a trust, or a foreign entity?

What are the terms of the Pakistan USD1 stablecoin MOU that Zachary Witkoff personally signed in January 2026, and did any coordination occur with Steve Witkoff's diplomatic portfolio or the Roosevelt Hotel redevelopment MOU that Steve brokered between Pakistan and the GSA?

What is the current status of the World Liberty Trust Company OCC charter application (2026-Charter-344521), and what regulatory analysis has been conducted regarding the proposed president being a Relative or Close Associate of a Politically Exposed Person as flagged by OpenSanctions?

Has ALT5 Sigma Corp's relationship with Jon Isaac's SEC fraud proceedings created any regulatory exposure for Zachary Witkoff as Chairman, and what due diligence was conducted before the $1.5 billion WLFI treasury strategy was routed through a company with this history?
